To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the amount of food consumed in a meal, and the rate of eating during a meal, depend on the size of the preceding meal; (b) the size of a meal is determined by its duration; (c) the duration of a meal is controlled by the rate of eating, which is in turn controlled by the size of the last preceding meal.
the metabolic theory of hunger is a theory about how the brain works, not about how the liver, pancreas, or muscles work.

1) the metabolic theory of hunger is not supported by any experimental paradigm that has been used to test it; 2) the theory that hunger is controlled by a metabolic sensor of glucose is not supported by the experimental evidence, and 3) the theory that adipose stores control hunger is not supported because it has not been tested.

the evidence for metabolic influences on hunger is weak.
